questions.q:
For hydrogen atom, the orbital/s with lowest energy is/are :
(A) 4 s
(B) $3 \mathrm{p}_x$
(C) $3 \mathrm{~d}_{x^2-y^2}$
(D) $3 \mathrm{~d}_{z^2}$
(E) $4 \mathrm{p}_z$

Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.solution:
For hydrogen atom and one electron species, the energy of orbitals is decided by the value of principal quantum number. Higher the value of principal quantum number, higher will be the energy of orbital.
$\therefore \quad(B),(C)$ and (D) have orbitals with the lowest energy.

questions.q: According to the wave-particle duality of matter by de-Broglie, which of the following graph plot presents most appropriate relationship between wavelength of electron <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mfenced><mi mathvariant="normal">λ</mi></mfenced></math> and momentum of electron <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mfenced><mi mathvariant="normal">p</mi></mfenced><mo>?</mo></math>
questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.solution:
According to the de-Broglie hypothesis according to which all matters have both particle and wave nature. where h= plank's constant, p=momentum, λ= wavelength of particle. This type of graph is called a rectangular hyperbola. As λ∝1p we will have a rectangular hyperbola.

λ=hpλ∝1p

⇒λp=h (constant)

So, the plot is a rectangular hyperbola.

questions.q:
Henry Moseley studied characteristic X-ray spectra of elements. The graph which represents his observation correctly is
Given v= Frequency of X-ray emitted
         Z= Atomic number
questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.solution:
Moseley's observation on characteristic X-ray spectra of elements relates frequency (v) of X-rays emitted to the atomic number by the following relation:
v=a(Z-b)
The plot of v vs Z is linear.

Based on this observation, the periodic law defined as the physical and chemical properties of the elements are periodic functions of their atomic numbers.

questions.q:
Given below are two statements :
Statement (I) : It is impossible to specify simultaneously with arbitrary precision, both the linear momentum and the position of a particle.
Statement (II) : If the uncertainty in the measurement of position and uncertainty in measurement of momentum are equal for an electron, then the uncertainty in the measurement of velocity is $\geqslant \sqrt{\frac{\mathrm{h}}{\pi}} \times \frac{1}{2 \mathrm{~m}}$.
In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below :
options: Statement I is false but Statement II is true
Both Statement I and Statement II are false
Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Statement I is true but Statement II is false
questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.solution:
According to Heisenberg's uncertainty principle, it is impossible to determine simultaneously the exact position and momentum of particle like electron
If 
$\begin{aligned} & \Delta p=\Delta x \\ & \Delta p \cdot \Delta x \geq \frac{h}{4 \pi} \\ &(\Delta p)^2 \geq \frac{h}{4 \pi} \\ & \Delta p \geq \sqrt{\frac{h}{\pi}} \times \frac{1}{2} \\ & m \Delta v \geq \sqrt{\frac{h}{\pi}} \times \frac{1}{2} \\ & \Delta v \geq \sqrt{\frac{h}{\pi}} \times \frac{1}{2 m}\end{aligned}$

questions.q: Consider an imaginary ion <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mmultiscripts><mi mathvariant="normal">X</mi><none/><mrow><mn>3</mn><mo>-</mo></mrow><mprescripts/><mn>22</mn><mn>48</mn></mmultiscripts></math>. The nucleus contains '<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">a</mi></math>'<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mo>%</mo></math> more neutrons than the number of electrons in the ion. The value of '<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">a</mi></math>' is
questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.solution:
X22483-

In an atomic representation XZA

Z is atomic number = 22

A is atomic mass number = 48.

No. of protons  = Z = 22

No. of neutrons =A-Z = 48-22 = 26

No. of electrons =P-charge = 22+3 = 25

% of extra neutrons than electrons =26-2525×100=4 % = a%

So, the value of a=4.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.solution:
The difference energy between two energy levels is 

∆E=2.18×10-18 1n12-1n22 J

1.47×10-17=2.18×10-18×(9)1(n)2-1(n+1)2

0.749=1n2-1(n+1)2

n = 1

Hence, the transition is taking place between 1→2, and it comes under Lymann series.

If we take 0.749≃0.75=34
